precision_rule.rule: Ada/Hopper (cc >= 8.9) with < 19.5 GiB -> HF FP8 W8A8 engine (engine_v4 'hf_fp8'); otherwise -> HF bf16 with batch size from a memory probe (rows x (P + max_new) x 147,456 B <= 0.8 x free VRAM). vLLM literal cell: bf16 only if the KV cache fits >= 4 sequences of 18,432 tokens, else Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 rev 220b46e3.
precision_rule.consequence: bf16: iteration-4 FP8 rows cannot be reused slot for slot; T1.3, TOPK10, NOVELTY and SEMSEED are rerun on D5 (P3); everything else from iteration 4 is carried flagged 'other engine'; the engine-check difference is reported as precision sensitivity

deviations.deviation: plan S0.8 commit #0 split by claim: commit0F (literal cell) is made before the first literal-cell sample; commit0C (Claim C) before the first decisive knob sample. Principle (g) 'committed before the first decisive sample of each claim' is kept.

format pilot v1 failed (EAP_A list parsed on 0-10% of rows, PSL_A on 0% for T2): the model obeyed the specification's final line 'Return only one ```python code block ...' and wrote code at once. The plan's ONE allowed wording revision was used before commit #1: PSL_A, EAP_A (and PSL_B) now state the step structure ('This is step 1 of 3: do not write any code in this step, and ignore the code-block instruction at the end of the task for now ...'); the specification tokens are unchanged. v1 results: predictions/format_pilot_v1.json.

with the revised wording the model copies the template's angle brackets literally ('<1>. <Quickselect>: <idea>'); parsers.py accepts that form (fixed before commit0C; pilot rerun; the first v2 pilot scored with the old parser is kept as predictions/format_pilot_v2_parser_v1.json).
PN direction seeded stable_seed(task, 'PN5', w, k) and SHARED by PN_a1, PN_a2 and PNPLAIN_a1 (exp19 used arm-specific seeds); dose and frame contrasts are exact at a fixed direction (plan S5).

precision rule (predictions/precision_rule.json): RTX 4090 24 GiB, cc 8.9 -> HF bf16 engine (not FP8 W8A8); iteration-4 FP8 rows are not reused slot for slot; T1.3, TOPK10 and NOVELTY are rerun on D5 and SEMSEED on T1/T2 (P3); every other iteration-4 knob is carried as 'other engine' in the knob table only.

vLLM U6 diagnostics: same seed twice gave identical 256-token text on 3/4 requests (no batch invariance below CC 9.0; the first run is a prefix-cache miss, the second a hit), and the processed logprobs with top_k=10 showed up to 12 finite entries (ties at the 10th value or logprob processing order); the literal cell's repeat at T 0.7 is the reported noise floor.
drop order applied before the full run: dropped=['IFG_paper', 'ND10_DMD_a2', 'ND10_PLAIN_PNPLAIN', 'P5', 'SEMSEED_rerun'], ND10 N30->20=True (extrapolated 9385s vs available 6752s)

analysis_c.py amended after commit0C, after a DRY RUN of the committed analysis on partial rows (P1 complete on D5, P2 in progress): arms with fewer than 30 rows on a D5 task (15 on ND10) are excluded from every hull and bootstrap and listed in results/incomplete_cells.json. Reason: the drop order removed IFG_paper after stage 100, leaving 2 rows per D5 task, and in the dry run those 2 rows lifted IFG's H5 on T03 from 1.10 (IFG_hot only) to 1.97. Direction of the effect: the amendment LOWERS IFG's price on T03 and so favours PN there; the unamended rule's result is reported as a sensitivity ('A1_not_applied'), and if the restore stage completes IFG_paper at N 50 the IFG dial is complete again.

the committed queue finished before the deadline; dropped cells are restored in reverse drop order until the same deadline (block_id 'restore:<step>'); analyses report the committed and the restored cell sets

analysis_c.py: per-task bootstrap replicates cached in results/boot_cache/<task>.json keyed by the sha256 of the task's rows, the class list and n_boot (fixed seeds -> identical replicates); computation only, no number changes. Lets the D5 bootstrap start while the restore stage still runs on ND10.

post hoc: base compositions of iteration 1 use an older label vocabulary; results/landings_harmonised.json recomputes the landing mass outside base support after mapping {'bellman_ford_spfa': 'bf_spfa', 'floyd_warshall': 'floyd', 'astar_greedy': 'astar_gbfs', 'dijkstra_unit': 'dijkstra'}; the committed (unharmonised) value is kept beside it
